briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East remains in a state of severe military escalation, marked by continuous multi-wave US airstrikes against Iranian military targets across several provinces, and direct Iranian retaliatory missile and drone attacks against US military facilities in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan. Iran's Health Ministry reported 35 fatalities and over 300 injuries from US attacks this month, underscoring the human cost of the escalating conflict.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran intensified significantly over the past 24 hours. The US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the completion of several waves of strikes, including a 90-minute morning wave targeting coastal defense and cruise missile sites on Greater Tunb Island, a 7-hour wave ending July 14 against dozens of military targets near the Strait of Hormuz and coastal areas, and a wave ending July 15 targeting command centers, air defense, missile/drone systems, and coastal surveillance facilities, including in Bandar Abbas. US forces also launched another wave of strikes "a short while ago" against Iranian military capabilities threatening vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, with US officials indicating these strikes aim to destroy capabilities prior to more complex operations and are "setting the stage."

Reported locations hit in Iran include Bandar Abbas (multiple times, with damage to a telecom tower reported, and near an airbase/airport), Qeshm Island (including the Susza fish powder factory), Sirik, Ahvaz (multiple strikes near Shahid Baghaei Hospital/cancer center, residential areas, military bases, pipe rolling mill), Chabahar (naval control tower, Ahmad Rizeh outpost), Konarak, Bampur (Iranشهر military barracks), Khondab, Semnan (unconfirmed reports of airport bombing), Parschin (air defense active, multiple explosions), Pakdasht, Borujerd, Khorramabad, and Manujan (Kerman). Iranian air defense systems were activated in Tehran, Parschin, Pakdasht, and Bandar Abbas. Iran claimed its IRGC Aerospace Force shot down a US MQ-9 drone over Andimeshk and a LUCAS drone near Bandar Abbas.

Iran launched retaliatory missile and drone strikes, claiming direct hits on US facilities in Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base, described as the largest-scale attack since the war began, with US air defenses reportedly failing to intercept), Kuwait (Ali Al Salem Air Base), and Jordan (Muwaffaq Al Salti Air Base in Azraq, with claims of Patriot system failure and satellite images showing damage to an anti-drone system and helicopter hangar at Prince Hassan Air Base). Jordan's military confirmed intercepting three missiles from Iran. Kuwait reportedly participated in the conflict, with an Iranian source claiming six missiles were launched from Kuwaiti territory (Um Qasr naval base area) over Iraqi airspace towards Iran.

The Iranian Health Ministry reported that US attacks this month have resulted in over 300 wounded and 35 killed, including two women and a teenager, with Hormozgan, Sistan and Baluchestan, and Khuzestan provinces suffering the heaviest losses. The Iranian Army reported 7 servicemen (permanent and conscript) killed in a US missile attack on a military barracks in Bampur, Sistan and Baluchestan.
Infrastructure damage includes the Susza fish powder factory, vicinity of Shahid Baghaei Hospital in Ahvaz (leading to evacuation of 211 pediatric cancer patients), and a telecom tower in Bandar Abbas. The US President Donald Trump threatened future strikes on Iranian power plants and bridges if a diplomatic resolution is not reached.

Internally, Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf stated that Iran never sought war but must always be ready, advocating for both military readiness and diplomacy. He warned that if the "Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)" with the US fails to benefit Iran, there is no reason for Tehran to adhere to it. The Foreign Ministry spokesman affirmed no plans to negotiate with the US as long as Washington violates its MoU commitments. The Army Spokesperson Akrami Nia declared the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the US recognizes Iran's lawful system of governance. Anti-regime channels reported protests in Tehran's market. The judiciary executed Mohammad Amini Dehagani (accused of arson during January protests) and Aref Khoshkar (from 2022 protests). A British citizen, Craig Foreman, received an additional 2-year prison sentence for media interviews, on top of a 10-year espionage conviction.

Economically, the Iranian Rial depreciated significantly, with the USD reaching 187,000 IRR, and gold at 18.41 million Toman per gram. Power outages in Tehran were linked to illegal cryptocurrency mining. Shipping companies are reportedly increasingly favoring Iranian-approved shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz due to US aggression.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations continued across multiple fronts. The IDF confirmed killing three armed Hezbollah operatives in a "military buffer zone" near Beit Yahoun in southern Lebanon, identified by the 869th Combat Intelligence Collection Unit and neutralized by the 401st Armored Brigade. In the Gaza Strip, the IDF announced the killing of Hassam Shafai, a Hamas terrorist involved in the October 7, 2023 abduction of Col. Asaf Hamami. Two Hamas Nukhba Force commanders, Ali Shamlakh and Nasser Louh, were killed in an Israeli strike in northern Gaza. The IDF also reported holding 67-70% of the Gaza Strip.

On the home front, Michael Katz, 82, died from injuries sustained from an Iranian missile in Haifa during the "Lion's Roar" operation. An Israeli female was injured by stone-throwing near Sinjil in the West Bank. Northern communities were warned of planned military activity between 02:00-04:00, with no change in instructions.

Politically, the "gender segregation bill in academia" was finally approved. The controversial "Judicial Advisor role weakening" bill passed its second and third readings (65-51), with opposition groups (Bar Association, Civil Rights Association, Movement for Quality Government) vowing Supreme Court challenges. The Supreme Court also suspended the "deferment of rabbinical students' arrests" law (draft exemption), prompting protests by Haredim and a letter signed by over 70 local authority heads against draft exemption laws. The "Combat Shock Victims Law" was approved. The Shin Bet will join the fight against crime in the Arab sector with a NIS 500 million budget and 130 new staff. The government approved up to NIS 55 million in compensation for Israeli airlines for empty flights during "Lion's Roar." MK Dan Illouz resigned from Likud to form a new party, "Israel First." Minister Ofir Sofer (Religious Zionism) announced his resignation from politics over Haredi draft disagreements. Foreign Minister Gideon Saar announced the renewal of full diplomatic relations with Colombia, including the opening of a Colombian embassy in Jerusalem. Shin Bet head Zini recommended lifelong security for Sara Netanyahu.

Civilian impacts included a 10-year-old injured in a Haifa car accident, a 15-year-old on an electric scooter injured in Jerusalem, and a 5-year-old killed by a car in Jerusalem. A criminal stun grenade incident occurred in Herzliya Pituach with no injuries. A fueling crisis at Ben Gurion Airport may lead to planes exceeding limits being removed.

Strategically, PM Netanyahu is scheduled to fly to the US, likely for a meeting with President Trump. Trump suggested Israel "exit parts of Lebanon and southern Syria" and considered giving a "green light" to "Al-Shara" (likely Abu Mohammad al-Julani) to "deal with Hezbollah."

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, IDF operations continued, resulting in the killing of Hassam Shafai, a Hamas terrorist involved in the October 7 abduction of Col. Asaf Hamami. Two Nukhba commanders, Ali Shamlakh and Nasser Louh, were also killed in northern Gaza. The IDF reportedly targeted a building in the Ma'azi refugee camp. Israel maintains control over 67-70% of the Gaza Strip.

In the West Bank, IDF troops arrested two wanted individuals in the Binyamin Brigade area, who were manufacturing explosives to target Israeli forces, and an arms dealer. Forces responded to stone-throwing incidents near Ma'ale Levona, resulting in an Israeli civilian injury and damage to two vehicles, leading to a cordon around Sinjil village.

Morocco formally joined the future Gaza stabilization force. Talks between Israel and Lebanon in Rome focused on implementing two pilot zones in southern Lebanon, with an announcement expected soon, including one area from which the IDF would withdraw. An aid worker involved in World Cup screenings in Gaza was reportedly killed in an Israeli strike.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations saw three armed operatives killed by the IDF near Beit Yahoun in southern Lebanon, within the Israeli-designated buffer zone. Lebanese media corroborated reports of Israeli strikes between Kounine and Beit Yahoun. PressTV also reported Israeli airstrikes on Baraachit and Beit Yahoun.
An Emirati news source (Aram News) reported that Hezbollah is preparing a plan for military escalation against Israel, including intense attacks on northern settlements, contingent on the level of US strikes in Iran or a green light from Washington for more intensive Israeli strikes deep inside Iran. Lebanon also reported arresting an individual for collaborating with Mossad and facilitating the assassinations of Hezbollah officials, including Fuad Shukr and Ibrahim Aqil.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Militia activity in Iraq saw Iraqi Hezbollah Battalions declaring immediate and decisive participation if a war erupts in Iran. The family of Abu al-Muhandis issued a warning to Trump of inevitable revenge for the killing of resistance commanders. Large-scale strikes reportedly targeted separatist terrorist cells in Erbil, Iraqi Kurdistan. A drone attack targeted the US military base near Erbil airport, raising smoke columns and activating ambulances, while the US Consulate's air defense system was activated. US warplanes were observed flying over Baghdad. Six missiles were reportedly launched from Kuwait over Iraqi airspace towards Iran. Explosions were also reported in Sulaymaniyah, Iraq. A US Congressman, Tim Burchett, publicly criticized the Iraqi Prime Minister, calling his speech "talking about nothing." The financial advisor to the Iraqi PM stated that sanctions on Hezbollah entities were in Iraq's interest.

GULF STATES
The Gulf region experienced direct impacts from the escalating conflict. Bahrain reported air raid sirens and explosions, with Iran claiming successful strikes on US facilities, particularly the Sheikh Isa Air Base, describing it as the largest attack since the war began and alleging failures of US air defense systems. Kuwait also reported explosions and Iranian claims of hits on US economic interests and facilities, including the Ali Al Salem Air Base, which hosts US military personnel. Furthermore, an Iranian source explicitly claimed Kuwait participated in the conflict by launching six missiles from its territory (Um Qasr naval base area) towards Iran. Jordan confirmed intercepting three missiles launched from Iran, while Iran claimed direct hits on the US Muwaffaq Al Salti Air Base in Azraq, alleging Patriot system failure, and satellite imagery reportedly showed damage to an anti-drone surveillance system and a helicopter hangar at Prince Hassan Air Base. Saudi Arabia extended the closure of Abha International Airport for three days following Yemeni attacks.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint. The US re-imposed a naval blockade on July 14 against vessels traveling to or from Iranian ports, disabling an empty Curacao-flagged oil tanker (M/T Belma) attempting to reach Kharg Island by firing Hellfire missiles at its smokestack after it ignored multiple warnings, and redirecting two other compliant commercial ships. The Iranian Army spokesperson, Brigadier General Akrami Nia, declared the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until the US recognizes Iran's "lawful system of governance" and an "Iranian-led framework" for the strategic waterway. Iran's Parliament Speaker Qalibaf similarly emphasized preserving "Iranian arrangements" over the Strait. The IRGC reportedly fired warning shots at two vessels attempting to pass without authorization in the last 24 hours. Notably, CBS News reported that shipping companies are increasingly favoring Iranian-approved shipping lanes due to US aggression in the Strait, leading to a plummet in overall traffic. President Trump is reportedly considering expanding military operations to seize Kharg Island.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Multiple Waves of US Strikes on Iran:** CENTCOM conducted continuous airstrikes targeting Iranian military command centers, air defense systems, missile/drone capabilities, and coastal surveillance facilities in several provinces, including Bandar Abbas, Ahvaz, Qeshm, and Chabahar.
2.  **Iranian Retaliatory Strikes on US Bases:** Iran claimed to have launched missile and drone attacks against US military facilities in Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base), Kuwait (Ali Al Salem Air Base), and Jordan (Muwaffaq Al Salti Air Base), with claims of successful impacts and failures of US air defense systems.
3.  **Significant Iranian Casualties:** Iran's Health Ministry reported 35 fatalities and over 300 injuries from US attacks this month. The Iranian Army reported 7 servicemen killed in a US missile attack on a military barracks in Bampur, Sistan and Baluchestan.
4.  **Strait of Hormuz Blockade and Interdictions:** The US re-imposed a naval blockade, disabling an oil tanker and redirecting two others. Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed until the US accepts its governance framework and its IRGC fired warning shots at two unauthorized vessels.
5.  **Israeli Soldier Convicted of Espionage for Iran:** An Israeli conscript soldier was sentenced to 5 years in prison for providing videos of missile interceptions and impacts to an Iranian handler during the June 2025 war.
6.  **Hamas and Hezbollah Commanders Eliminated:** IDF operations in Gaza killed three Hamas commanders, including one involved in the October 7 abduction of Col. Asaf Hamami. Three armed Hezbollah operatives were also eliminated in southern Lebanon.
7.  **US Escalation Threats:** President Trump threatened to expand future attacks on Iran to include power plants and bridges if a diplomatic deal is not reached, and discussed seizing Kharg Island in a White House Situation Room meeting.
8.  **Colombia Renews Ties with Israel:** Colombia agreed to renew full diplomatic relations with Israel and open an embassy in Jerusalem.
9.  **Israeli "Judicial Advisor" Law Passed:** The controversial bill to weaken the role of the Attorney General was approved in Israel, prompting strong domestic opposition and legal challenges.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high. The continuous and expanding nature of US airstrikes, coupled with President Trump's explicit threats against Iranian critical infrastructure (power plants, bridges) and discussions about ground operations (Kharg Island), signal a potential shift towards a much broader conflict. Iran's direct retaliatory strikes on US military facilities in Gulf states and Jordan demonstrate its willingness and capability to project force regionally, increasing the likelihood of further tit-for-tat actions. The declaration by Iraqi Hezbollah Battalions to immediately join a war in Iran, and Hezbollah's reported preparations for escalation against Israel, indicate a potential regionalization of the conflict. Active flashpoints include southern Iran, the Strait of Hormuz (with ongoing naval blockades and interdictions), US bases in Iraq, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan, and the Israel-Lebanon border. Military postures are hardening: the US is engaged in continuous air/naval strikes and considering ground operations, while Iran is actively using air defense and conducting retaliatory strikes, with its IRGC spokesman indicating a "next phase" of operations. Red lines include Iran's sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz and US freedom of navigation, with new US red lines explicitly drawn at Iran's failure to negotiate, which could lead to attacks on its energy and infrastructure.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture is one of sustained military pressure and economic coercion. Multiple waves of airstrikes against Iran's military capabilities continued, alongside the re-imposition of a naval blockade on Iranian ports. The State Department issued a broad travel warning for numerous countries including Iran, Iraq, and Lebanon. President Trump's statements fluctuated between claims of Iran wanting to meet, threats of expanding strikes to critical infrastructure (power plants, bridges) if no deal is reached, and considering regime change in Iran as possible. Vice President Vance, however, expressed skepticism about military solutions for Strait of Hormuz navigation and the effectiveness of regime change operations via military interventions.

Gulf states are directly impacted. Bahrain and Kuwait reported explosions on their territories, with Iran claiming successful missile strikes on US military bases there. Jordan confirmed intercepting Iranian missiles and also reportedly sustained damage to a US base. Saudi Arabia extended the closure of Abha International Airport following Yemeni attacks. Russia expressed strong concern over the escalating conflict in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz, calling for a return to negotiations and emphasizing the ineffectiveness of force-based solutions. Colombia announced a renewal of full diplomatic relations with Israel and plans to open an embassy in Jerusalem. Malaysia's Prime Minister stated that any Israelis found in the country would be immediately deported.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions and unverified claims exist across the intelligence feed. Iranian sources (PressTV, SharghDaily) reported civilian casualties and damage to civilian infrastructure (e.g., Ahvaz cancer hospital, Qeshm fish factory), which CENTCOM explicitly denied, stating only military targets were engaged. Iranian claims of US Patriot failures in Jordan and general US air defense failures in Bahrain remain unconfirmed by US or allied sources. Initial reports of explosions in Tehran by "omid dana" were later retracted or unconfirmed by the same source, highlighting the fluid and often unreliable nature of real-time battlefield reporting. Similarly, SharghDaily first reported explosions in Bushehr and Shiraz, only to later attribute them to routine industrial activity. The claim by Naya and Kianmeli1 that Kuwait launched six missiles towards Iran over Iraqi airspace is a highly significant and unverified assertion that, if true, would profoundly alter the regional dynamics.

Propaganda indicators are evident from all sides. Iranian media consistently frames US actions as "criminal," "unprovoked aggression," and violations of international agreements, while presenting Iranian actions as justified retaliation. US President Trump's statements about Iran wanting to negotiate or his ability to unilaterally end attacks appear to be aimed at political positioning. His suggestion to "greenlight" a Syrian extremist leader to "deal with Hezbollah" is a highly controversial and unverified proposal with significant geopolitical implications. A notable typo appears in a Mannie's War Room report, stating Hamas returned Asaf Hamami's body in "November 2025" instead of an earlier date, likely 2023 or 2024. Reporting gaps include the lack of independent verification for casualty figures from Iran, precise damage assessments of US bases, and detailed information about the "Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)" and "Iranian arrangements" over the Strait of Hormuz, which are central to Iran's diplomatic stance.
